subsystems.name: Air intake and mover
subsystems.role: draws ambient air across the moisture-capturing surface.

subsystems.name: Moisture capture
subsystems.role: turns airborne vapour into liquid water or binds it to a sorbent.

subsystems.name: Cooling or regeneration loop
subsystems.role: provides the cold surface, or the heat that releases water from the sorbent.
parts: heater or solar thermal loop for desiccant regeneration

subsystems.name: Water handling and storage
subsystems.role: moves and holds the produced water.

subsystems.name: Water treatment
subsystems.role: makes the water safe and pleasant to drink.

subsystems.name: Power and controls
subsystems.role: runs the cycle and adapts it to changing weather.

buildSteps.title: Size the machine to the climate
buildSteps.detail: Estimate how much water the local temperature and humidity can yield, and how much energy that will take. Output falls steeply as air gets drier.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the heat exchangers
buildSteps.detail: Cooling coils are made from corrosion-resistant metal with closely spaced fins to maximise contact with the air.

buildSteps.title: Build the refrigeration circuit
buildSteps.detail: A compressor, condenser, expansion device and evaporator are assembled and charged with refrigerant.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the sorbent path (sorption type)
buildSteps.detail: Desiccant material — silica gel, zeolite or a metal-organic framework — is packed into a bed or coated onto a rotating wheel.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the air path
buildSteps.detail: Fan, filter and coils or sorbent wheel are mounted so air passes through in the intended order.

buildSteps.title: Add collection and storage
buildSteps.detail: Condensate or released water is collected, pumped to a tank and protected from contamination.

buildSteps.title: Install treatment and controls
buildSteps.detail: Filters, UV lamp, sensors and the control board are wired so the unit starts, stops and self-regulates.

buildSteps.title: Test output and water quality
buildSteps.detail: The unit is run across humidity ranges and the water is tested for minerals, microbes and taste before potable use.

prerequisites.why: the standard way to cool a surface below the dew point; mature but energy-hungry.
silica gel and zeolites work but need heat to regenerate; advanced metal-organic frameworks promise better uptake in dry air.
they determine how much water you get per kilowatt-hour.
collected water can pick up dust, metals and microbes and must be filtered or disinfected.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap low-carbon electricity or solar heat
prerequisites.why: the process is far more energy-intensive than treating piped or groundwater, so its climate benefit depends on the power source.

pathway.milestone: commercial condensation units for humid climates, emergency relief and off-grid homes
pathway.unlocks: drinking water where humidity is high and other sources are absent.

pathway.milestone: sorption units driven by solar heat or waste heat instead of compressors
pathway.unlocks: lower electricity demand and better output in moderately dry air.

pathway.milestone: metal-organic framework harvesters that pull useful water from desert air
pathway.unlocks: water production in arid regions, demonstrated in laboratories and early field trials.

pathway.milestone: building-integrated and farm-scale systems paired with renewable power
pathway.unlocks: a supplementary water supply that does not depend on rain, rivers or aquifers.
